title: Multiple Regression Model in Analysis Effect of Various Additional Dietary Fibre Sources in the Diet of Broiler Chickens as a Factor Affected Development of Gastrointestinal Tract
content: The aim of the experiment was to investigate the effect of using 50% of wheat grain in the diet with 3% of various structural components on the development of the gastrointestinal tract of broiler chickens and related with it organs and to attempt to modelling this phenomenon on data obtained from chickens at 35 days of age using multiple regression equations. The use of various structural components: oat hull (OH), sunflower hull (SH), sugar beet pulp (SBP) and wheat bran (WB) at the level of 3% of the diet affects the digestive processes in the gastrointestinal tract of broiler chickens, but also causes a change in the length of intestinal sections or the weight of organs related to the digestive tract, which can be taken into account during the preparation of an experimental model that is at least partially applicable to transferring the results to human studies. The use of OH and SH (3%) in the diet results in a significantly higher body weight (p< 0.05) of birds compared to SBP and WB. OH in the diet significantly increased (p< 0.01) the weight of the gizzard of chickens compared to the other groups differentiated by the type of additional dietary fibre apart from SH. On the other hand, the weight of the proventriculus in chickens fed a diet containing OH was significantly lower than in the case of SBP (p< 0.05). The use of SH in the diet caused a significant decrease (p< 0.01) in the heart weight of chickens. OH in the diet also significantly increased (p< 0.05) the length of the small and large intestines and the total length of the intestines compared to other additional sources of fibre in the diet. Correlation analysis showed a significant average positive relationship (p< 0.05) between the content of TDF in the diet and the weight of the gizzard and indicated a significant positive correlation between the length of the jejunum and the remaining sections of the intestines. In turn, modelling for regression equations indicated a significant effect (p< 0.01) of all independent variables on jejunal, ileal, caecal length and liver weight. Further studies are necessary with separate models in experiments with soluble and insoluble fibre, which will increase the accuracy of determining the effect of these types of fibre and will also allow for the preparation of an experimental plan for variable proportions in the future.
